notes:
Summary: large defense contractor with classified-document search and assistant needs. Strong initial interest in Redwood Private for secure inference. Key reqs: fully air-gapped deployment where customer owns hardware and operator keys, HSM integration (FIPS), no external control plane access, strict audit/retention controls. 

What happened: ran a short POC in Redwood Private staging (non-production, customer data redacted). Customer's security team dug in and confirmed their policy disallows any externally-managed control plane and requires supplier to provide on-site appliance or signed handover of hardware. Redwood Private offers customer-managed VPC and a private control plane option, but platform team cannot support the customer's requirement for physically air-gapped hardware installed and operated solely by the customer in their secure facility. Competitor (OnPremAI Solutions) proposed an appliance + on-site installation + classified-data handling pedigree and got the procurement fast-tracked. Budget was reallocated to hardware acquisition.

Signals: repeated phrase from CISO: "no external network / no outbound control plane under any circumstances"; legal flagged indemnity around on-site installs. Internal champion (Head of AI Ops) left during review cycle (reorg) — lost momentum.

Action items / next steps: closed-lost; AE to send loss-review slide + security FAQ to product & infra for lessons learned. Mark as potential win-back in 6-12 months when hardware refresh cycle begins. Keep watch on any RFP updates.

Quote from customer during final call: "We need an appliance we can plug into our classified network, no exceptions."
reason_lost: Customer required fully air-gapped on-prem appliance and ownership of hardware/control plane (HSM/FIPS) that Redwood could not deliver under current private offering; competitor delivered appliance+on-site certification; budget shifted to hardware purchase.
